Hi Sarah, come in.
I thought it would be useful to have Miss Reyes here as well to hear about your survey.
Good morning, Sarah.
Hello, OK, so as I was saying, Ms Reyes.
Sarah and her team at our IT Club online magazine have been doing a survey where there have been asking students about mobile phone use during the school day.
So Sarah, maybe you can give us some more details.
Yes, and thank you for seeing me today.
Well, we're writing an article about the survey and we thought it would be good to include your comments as well in the article.
OK, fine. the first issue we asked about was when we can use our phones during the school day.
At the moment we're only allowed to use our phones until 8: 45 in the morning and we can’t use our phones during class.
Oh, I thought you could use your phones until 8: 55.
No, only until 8: 45.
OK, my mistake.
So, students think the policy is outdated.
What do you mean by outdated?
What would students like to change?
Well, I think they'd like the policy to be more flexible.
I see. And this is the feedback from the school survey you did?
Sorry, can you tell us more about it?
Yes, we did a survey to ask students about why they want to use their phones and lots of students responded.
We had from 64 junior students and 150 senior students, so that’s 214 students in total 214!
That's a lot of responses!
I'm impressed. Well done to the IT Club, What were the main requests from students from the survey then?
Well, the most popular requests were that students would like to use their phones for 30 minutes at lunchtime and when walking between classes.
Walking between classes!
Absolutely not! Students would never arrive on time!
Half an hour at lunchtime is fair.
but certainly not between classes.
There's just enough time and normal.
Oh, OK. What else?
Oh yeah, they also said they'd like permission to use their phones during physics and language classes Why during those classes specifically?
Well, they'd like to use them in physics classes so they can use calculator apps, and they want to use them in language classes for online dictionaries.
They said they think this would be really helpful for their studies, especially for students who are preparing for exams.
What do you think about that idea.
Miss Reyes? Hmm, I don't agree that you need them in physics classes scientific calculators are better than phone calculators.
But, yes, they could be useful in language classes.
I think you're absolutely right about both points, Ms Reyes.
There's no need to use phones during physics class, but using them for online dictionaries is definitely a good idea.
OK. Were there any other issues that came up from the survey?
Yes, there was one other request, Students aren't allowed to charge their phone batteries in classrooms so they'd like to ask for a battery charging station.
A battery charging station.
That's actually a good idea.
would have to think carefully about where to put it.
Did they have any suggestions?
The students, I mean.
Well one place they said was, you know, in the corridor next to the playground.
Hmm, I'm not so sure about that.
There could be problems with the security with that.
Yes, I tend to agree with Miss Chan I'm afraid.
So that’s out as a location then but I still think it’s a good idea.
Sarah, did you have another suggestion for a location?
The other one was the library.
OK. Yeah, that might work.
It’s certainly popular at lunchtime.
Yeah, that’s a good idea.
We'll look into it definitely.
OK, well I'll look forward to reading the article in the online magazine.
